diagnosis.summary: The nightly run f70b6840 for 2026-10-01 failed at ingest because upstream renamed orders.order_total to total_amount. That rename is the only header change, and the format and meaning look the same in the rows I could check. I've proposed an ingest column mapping (orders: total_amount -> order_total), which still needs to be checked on the rerun. I found no upstream changelog; if this rename turns out not to be deliberate, tell the app team.

root_cause.explanation: Starting with the 2026-10-01 delivery, the upstream orders.csv has the column total_amount where the raw contract expects order_total. Ingest has no mapping (config is empty), so the schema check failed with 'missing order_total, unexpected total_amount'. The values look unchanged in the rows I could see: plain 2-decimal numbers, and totals equal to the sum of line items, as on 09-30. But only 2 orders on 10-01 were fully checked, because the inspect tool shows only a few lines of each file.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed for 2026-10-01: missing column order_total, unexpected column total_amount. The previous runs succeeded.
No column mapping exists in the ingest config.
The 10-01 header differs from the contract and the 09-30 file only by the order_total -> total_amount rename. The number format is unchanged.
On 09-30 every order_total equals the sum of its line items. In the few 10-01 rows that could be fully checked, total_amount matches the same way.
The runbooks say a rename with the same meaning should be fixed with apply_column_mapping, not redelivery.

alternatives_considered: request_upstream_redelivery: rejected. A deliberate header rename is not a one-off delivery problem.

escalate_to_owner(upstream_app_team) over a possible change in meaning: not chosen. The format is unchanged and the checked totals equal the line-item sums, though only 2 orders on 10-01 were fully checked.
ignore_extra_columns(total_amount): rejected. It would leave the required order_total column missing.
The orders row count fell 4.6% (461 to 440): treated as normal daily variation. The items-per-order ratio is similar.

proposal.rationale: Upstream renamed orders.order_total to total_amount starting with the 2026-10-01 delivery. That is the only header difference, and the value format and meaning look unchanged: plain 2-decimal numbers, and the spot-checked totals equal the sum of their line items, as every order did on 09-30. The runbooks say a rename with unchanged meaning should be handled with apply_column_mapping, not redelivery. After the mapping, rerun the pipeline and confirm that order_total for 10-01 still matches the line-item sums.

applied: ingest now reads raw.orders.order_total from upstream column 'total_amount'
